hints.title: Read the theorem exactly
hints.body: The stated theorem uses an upper limit equal to the differentiation variable. Check separately how the theorem is being used in each displayed line.
hints.recap: Read the theorem’s conditions before substituting.
hints.pitfall: The integration variable and the variable controlling an endpoint have different roles.
hints.pause: List the upper limits and the variable of differentiation in each application of the theorem.

recall.reminder: For a fixed lower bound and upper endpoint x, the derivative of accumulated area equals the integrand at x.

hints.title: Check the integrals by direct evaluation
hints.body: You can check the claimed derivatives using the power rule: first evaluate each definite integral with antiderivative t33. Then differentiate the resulting polynomial in x.
hints.recap: Evaluate first, then differentiate; this provides an independent check.
hints.pitfall: Substitute both bounds before simplifying the definite integral.
hints.pause: Evaluate each integral and differentiate your resulting expressions.

recall.reminder: Integrate powers and substitute the actual upper and lower bounds.

hints.title: Find the earliest discrepancy
hints.body: Compare the displayed argument with your independent calculations, starting at the first equality. Separate a justified identity from a rule being applied outside its stated form.
hints.recap: Every step before the first error must have a valid justification.
hints.pitfall: A later line can follow correctly from an earlier incorrect expression.
hints.pause: Identify the first unsupported step and explain the precise mismatch.

recall.reminder: The first invalid line must be preceded only by justified lines.

solution:
Line I correctly uses additivity of signed integrals. Line II correctly applies FTC with upper limit x.

For line III, direct evaluation gives ∫02xt2dt=(2x)33=8x33, whose derivative is 8x2, not 4x2. Thus line III is the first error.

As a complete check, ∫x2xt2dt=[t33]x2x=7x33, so its derivative is 7x2. Equivalently subtract the corrected derivatives 8x2−x2.

Answer D: the first error is on line III.
